data.headline: Nunnells Sits Atop The Throne, Everyone Else Fights For Scraps
data.deck: The Shart Bowl loser gets an away game and a chance to do it all again, God help her.
body: One week into this dumpster fire and nunnells already looks like the team to beat. 169.86 points, Manager of the Week, a 77.5 playoff mark, the whole package. Next up for the throne room tour is Bibi's Ballers 69, a LoRdAcE1848 squad that dropped 146.86 in a loss and still has to go on the road against the hottest team in the league. Good luck with that.

Right behind nunnells sits 50 Shades of Zay, tripnistico's crew that put up 162.8 in week one and now walks into a matchup with Romo911, the DFWGilly outfit that just hung 153.92 on Victorious Secrets. Two teams that can flat out score meet in week two and something has to give.

Now for the sad part. Tayodin's Victorious Secrets just posted 63.04, the lowest number on the board, got run over by DFWGilly, and got crowned this week's Shart Bowl loser for it. The reward for that performance is a date with bearcat2789's Hog tied and deep fried, a team that just lost the closest game of the week by a single point despite Josh Allen throwing for 35.66. One of these teams needs saving. Neither one inspires much confidence right now.
Everybody else in the middle is still figuring out who they are. Buckle up.

data.headline: Caleb Williams Torches League, LoRdAcE1848 Torches Himself Anyway
data.deck: The top scorers of Week 1, and a reminder that stacking studs means nothing if your bench is a crime scene
body: Caleb Williams went off for 37.26 points in Week 1, the single best individual performance in the entire league, and he did it wearing a Bears uniform, which should honestly be studied by scientists. That number belonged to SexRobot69, who also rostered Derrick Henry putting up 35.3 of his own. Two guys on one roster combining for numbers like that and First Down Syndrome still only found 156.06 on the scoreboard, which tells you everything about how deep the waiver churn is going to get this year.

Josh Allen dropped 35.66 for bearcat2789, and it still wasn't enough, because Hog tied and deep fried lost by a single point in the closest game of the week. Put up 35.66 from your quarterback and lose anyway. That's not bad luck, that's a horror movie.
Kenneth Walker chipped in 34.1 for tripnistico, quietly helping 50 Shades of Zay roll to 162.8 on the week without much drama.

And then there's LoRdAcE1848, who somehow had both Jalen Coker at 33.8 and Jahmyr Gibbs at 33.6 on the same roster, two legitimate monster games, and still walked away with a loss. Bibi's Ballers 69 put up 146.86 and lost. Two 33-plus performances and an L. Some men just weren't built to win, and this week LoRdAcE1848 proved it in stereo.

data.headline: The Trade Desk Is Closed for Business
data.deck: Week 1 came and went without a single trade getting done, which honestly says more about this league than any blockbuster ever could.
body: Nothing. Zero. Not a single transaction hit the wire this week. Fourteen managers, and not one of you had the stones to pick up the phone.

You'd think somebody watching Victorious Secrets put up 63.04 points would have called Tayodin with an offer, any offer, just to be nice. Nope. Left him twisting in the wind at the bottom of the standings with nobody even pretending to want his players.

Meanwhile nunnells is sitting up top with 169.86 points looking untouchable and not one rival tried to buy a piece of that roster before it gets more expensive. First Down Syndrome just dropped 156.06 and Bibi's Ballers 69 still lost with 146.86 on the board, and somehow neither manager thought a trade might fix what's broken. LoRdAcE1848 watched Jalen Coker go for 33.8 and Jahmyr Gibbs go for 33.6 in the same losing effort and apparently decided that roster is just fine as is.

This is a league full of bubble teams according to the odds, half of you sitting in the 50s and 60s for playoff chances, and the trade market is a ghost town. Get it together by Week 2 or this column is just going to be me screaming into a phone that nobody answers.
data.signOff: See you next week, you spineless non-negotiators.

data.headline: One Point Separates Jackson Off From The Deep Fryer
data.deck: Bheinzeyo escapes bearcat2789 by a single point despite Josh Allen going off, because fantasy football does not care about your quarterback's feelings.
body: Final score: 123.96 to 122.96. Say that number out loud a few times and let it ruin your week the way it ruined bearcat2789's.

Hog tied and deep fried had every reason to feel good walking into Sunday. Josh Allen threw for 35.66 points wearing the bearcat2789 crest, the kind of quarterback week that usually wins you the whole matchup by itself. Instead it won him nothing. Bheinzeyo's Jackson Off squad matched him stride for stride and then found one extra point somewhere in the couch cushions to close it out 123.96 to 122.96, a margin so thin you could floss with it.

This is the cruelty of Week 1. You can get a monster quarterback performance, you can do everything a fantasy manager is supposed to do, and you still end up 0-1 in the standings because somebody else's flex guy had a better Sunday afternoon by the width of a single point. Bearcat2789 will replay this one in his head all week wondering where that last point went. A different flex decision. A kicker who misses an extra point instead of hitting it. Anything, and this recap has a different headline.

Bheinzeyo does not care about any of that. Jackson Off takes the win, takes the 1-0, and moves on with 123.96 points for and a story he will tell for the rest of the season every time bearcat2789 brings up bad beats. That is how margins like this work. Nobody remembers the effort. Everybody remembers the number.

data.headline: Around The League: Blowouts, A Shart, And Nunnells Showing Off
data.deck: Six more games happened while everyone was busy watching a one point classic. Some of these ended before halftime.
body: Let's blow through the carnage while the Jackson Off game of the week soaks up all the attention it doesn't deserve.
Chase Browns with Downs took care of business against ItsYaBoyJack, 118 to 95.2. JPellett3 didn't need style points, just needed ItsYaBoyJack to keep being ItsYaBoyJack.
Romo911's DFWGilly turned Victorious Secrets into an actual crime scene, 153.92 to 63.04. Tayodin's 63.04 wasn't just a loss, it was this week's Shart, and it wasn't close.
Nunnells went nuclear on Burrowed Alive, 169.86 to 77.46. That's the highest score in the league this week and sebeatty had zero answer for it. Manager of the Week, no debate, no committee needed.
50 Shades of Zay held off BedBathNBIJAN22, 162.8 to 142.9, with Kenneth Walker going for 34.1 and doing most of the heavy lifting for tripnistico.

First Down Syndrome survived Bibi's Ballers 69, 156.06 to 146.86, in the closest thing this recap has to a fistfight. LoRdAcE1848 got 33.8 out of Jalen Coker and 33.6 out of Jahmyr Gibbs and still lost, because SexRobot69 was sitting on Caleb Williams dropping 37.26 and Derrick Henry adding 35.3 on top of it. Sometimes you bring a knife and the other guy brought two howitzers.
Zyn-bo Squisher steamrolled The Bhayshul Olympics, 116.22 to 75.3. Mattmcneese's season opener went about as well as the team name suggests these things usually go.

So that's Week 1. Seven winners feeling great about themselves, seven losers already refreshing the waiver wire. See you in the standings, where nunnells is sitting at the top looking real comfortable.

data.headline: Week 1 Waiver Wire: Unproven Names, Real Numbers
data.deck: Nobody knows who actually got picked up off waivers this week, but plenty of dudes had performances that scream do not cut me.
body: Look, the packet does not tell me who dropped who for who, so I cannot sit here and pretend I watched fourteen men frantically refresh their app at 4am Wednesday. What I can tell you is which names showed up on scoreboards like they had something to prove, and if any of these guys were sitting on your bench because you did not trust them, congratulations on the free education.

LoRdAcE1848 got a two piece from his own roster, Jalen Coker dropping 33.8 and Jahmyr Gibbs adding 33.6, and somehow still lost to SexRobot69 by 9.2. That is not a waiver wire story, that is a cautionary tale about depth not mattering when your opponent has Caleb Williams throwing for 37.26 and Derrick Henry running for 35.3 on the same roster. Absolutely disgusting stat line for one team.

tripnistico rode Kenneth Walker's 34.1 to a win over BedBathNBIJAN22, margin of 19.9, and now sits at 1-0 with 162.8 points for. If Walker was a speculative add, tripnistico deserves a parade. If he was rostered day one, tripnistico deserves nothing, we take our credit seriously here.
bearcat2789 got 35.66 out of Josh Allen and still found a way to lose by exactly 1 point. Some performances pay off. Some just make the loss hurt more.

data.headline: Nunnells Drops 169.86 On A Corpse
data.deck: The week's top score came against a guy who forgot to set a lineup with a pulse, but a big number is a big number.
body: Let's give the man his flowers. Nunnells put up 169.86 points in Week 1, the best score in all of Squirtnite FFL, and nobody else in this league sniffed it. That's a legitimately nasty output for opening weekend, the kind of number that makes the other thirteen teams check their own roster and quietly weep.

Here's the thing though. The victim was sebeatty and Burrowed Alive, who mustered all of 77.46 points and lost by 92.4. That's not a fantasy matchup, that's a mugging. Nunnells could have started three tight ends and a punter and still cruised, because whatever Burrowed Alive rolled out there Week 1 was closer to a bye week than a lineup.

So yes, put nunnells at the top of the standings at 1-0 and the top of the power rankings at rank 1. Just know the algorithm isn't fully buying it either, nunnells sits at a modest 77.5 percent to make the playoffs, tagged Bubble right alongside a bunch of teams that didn't score anywhere close to 169.86. Big week, real number, real trophy. Just maybe find a stiffer test before we start measuring anybody for a bye.
data.signOff: See you next week, when somebody else gets to feel like a genius for one Sunday.

data.headline: Week 1 Power Rankings: One Point Decided Everything Except The Things That Weren't Close At All
data.deck: Fourteen teams, one bloodbath, one heartbreak by a single point, and one shart so violent it needs its own zip code.
body: Week 1 is done and the league already looks exactly like you'd expect if you've met these idiots before. Somebody scored 169.86 and somebody scored 63.04 in the same week of the same sport, which tells you everything about the gap between preparation and vibes in this league. Here's how everybody stacks up.

1. nunnells (nunnells) — Dropped 169.86 on poor Burrowed Alive and walked away with Manager of the Week. This is either a statement or a fluke, and honestly nobody in this league can tell the difference until Week 12.
2. 50 Shades of Zay (tripnistico) — 162.8 points behind Kenneth Walker's 34.1, which is a hell of a way to open a season you named after a BDSM joke about a running back.

3. First Down Syndrome (SexRobot69) — 156.06 points powered by Caleb Williams throwing for 37.26 and Derrick Henry running for 35.3. Two absurd stat lines in one lineup and the team is still named that.
4. Romo911 (DFWGilly) — Put up 153.92 and turned Victorious Secrets into a crime scene, winning by 90.88. Tony would be proud, mostly of the destruction.
5. Jackson Off (Bheinzeyo) — Won the closest game in the building, 123.96 to 122.96, a margin of exactly 1. Somewhere bearcat2789 is throwing his remote at a wall right now.
6. Chase Browns with Downs (JPellett3) — 118 points, a workmanlike win over ItsYaBoyJack. Nothing sexy, nothing broken, just a W with no adjectives attached.
7. Zyn-bo Squisher (jwslaney) — Rolled to 116.22 and buried The Bhayshul Olympics by 40.92. Solid debut for a team named after a nicotine pouch and violence.
8. Bibi's Ballers 69 (LoRdAcE1848) — Scored 146.86 with Jalen Coker going for 33.8 and Jahmyr Gibbs going for 33.6 and STILL lost. That's not bad luck, that's a bye week disguised as a roster.
9. BedBathNBIJAN22 (BedBathNBIJAN22) — 142.9 points and a loss by 19.9. Solid stat line, wrong week to have it.
10. Hog tied and deep fried (bearcat2789) — Josh Allen went off for 35.66 and it still wasn't enough, losing by the margin 1. This is the fantasy equivalent of getting dumped over text.
11. ItsYaBoyJack (ItsYaBoyJack) — 95.2 points, lost by 22.8. Forgettable in a league that will not let you forget anything.
12. Burrowed Alive (sebeatty) — 77.46 points, lost by 92.4 to nunnells. Buried alive was right there in the name, congrats on the foreshadowing.
13. The Bhayshul Olympics (mattmcneese) — 75.3 points, lost by 40.92. The opening ceremony was rough.
14. Victorious Secrets (Tayodin) — 63.04 points, the Shart of the Week, beaten by DFWGilly by 90.88. There is nothing victorious about this and the secret is out.

data.headline: Victorious Secrets Reveals Absolutely Nothing Victorious
data.deck: Tayodin opens the season by getting more embarrassed than his own team name promised.
body: Let's start with the corpse. Tayodin's Victorious Secrets put up 63.04 points in Week 1, which is the kind of number you post when you're trying to lose a bet on purpose. There is no lace, no mystery, no secret here. Everybody saw everything, and what they saw was ugly.

On the other side of that matchup, DFWGilly's Romo911 dropped 153.92 and turned this into a 90.88 margin bloodbath. That's not a fantasy loss, that's a public execution with a scoreboard. Tayodin didn't lose a fantasy game so much as he got dragged behind a truck for four quarters while everyone else watched and ate popcorn.
